speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for your patience. To begin my assessment, can you describe the appearance, texture, and any changes you've noticed in the specific skin lesions you are concerned about?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis of pneumonia doesn't align with skin lesions; let's focus on the penile and finger findings. Have these lesions appeared suddenly or developed slowly over weeks or months?

REQUEST TEST: TSH, ESR, CRP, VDRL

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the non-healing, crusty nature of the lesions on both the penile shaft and your finger, have you noticed any bleeding, ulceration, or rapid growth in these areas?

REQUEST TEST: Tumor Markers (CEA, CA-15-3, CA-19-9)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and digit), secondary to chronic inflammation (Bowen's disease/keratoacanthoma).
